headlines.headline: First 30 minutes: the CPI repricing is trading, not just futures — Nasdaq opened -0.6% (QQQ -0.6%), S&P 500 -0.4% (SPY -0.3%), while the Dow ticked up ~0.1-0.3% as energy (Chevron +1%) masked tech weakness. 10Y at 5.29-5.32% (+~10bps vs Tuesday's close); October hike odds jumped to 44% (Investopedia) - 51.5% (Barron's, 'could be a coin flip') from ~22% pre-print.
headlines.why_it_matters: Headline printed 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected and core 2.6% vs 2.5% — the October hike went from 1-in-5 to a coin flip within the first hour of the print, so every rate-sensitive bid is being repriced live at the open.

headlines.headline: NVDA down ~1.8% to $224.38 in early trading (from a $228.52 prior close) with no company-specific news — part of the broad AI/tech rate repricing after the hot CPI.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rates repricing hits duration-heavy AI names first: NVDA bleeding with no news means the move is about the discount rate, not the story — carried over: NVDA's China data-center AI-chip share fell to 34% (IDC, H1 2026) while Huawei climbed to 28%.

headlines.headline: Memory story splits overnight: KOSPI rebounded ~2% (Samsung +3%, SK Hynix +2-3%) on bargain hunting after Tuesday's brutal foreign selloff (Samsung -7.4%, SK Hynix -10.1%); KB Securities says the drop formed a 'second trough' on flows, not fundamentals. US-listed memory names still soft; the CXMT 4F2 claim remains unverified.
headlines.why_it_matters: The fragility has moved from the claim to the lag — if Korean names found a floor on valuation while US names keep bleeding, the asymmetry favors dip-buyers; but the whole thesis resets the moment the CXMT claim gets validated or debunked.

headlines.headline: Cybersecurity names sold off after The Information reported OpenAI is in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits: Palo Alto down ~3% to near $386 (IBD's live blog had it -6% in morning action), CrowdStrike -2%, Fortinet -3%+, Okta and Zscaler also lower.
headlines.why_it_matters: This is the March fear redux — AI model-makers competing with incumbents — landing right into an already risk-off tape; the report is single-source, so the move is headline-fragile.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave plunged ~13.6% to $67.21 in early trading, extending a 5-day drawdown of nearly -27% (Finnhub); no fresh company-specific catalyst was sourced this morning.
headlines.why_it_matters: No catalyst means this is repricing, not reaction — AI-infrastructure names are where hot CPI (higher-for-longer) and AI-capex anxiety meet, so CRWV is the tape's rate-sensitivity proxy.

headlines.headline: Bank of America an early loser after the open (down ~4-5%) on the $1.2B AML fine and the adjusted EPS $1.08 vs $1.10 miss; BlackRock held its +5% gain (adjusted EPS $15.93 vs $14.32, $15.49T AUM).
headlines.why_it_matters: Bank prints are holding their premarket direction through the CPI repricing — earnings-wave stocks are trading on their merits while the index trades on the Fed.

headlines.headline: Chevron +1% toward new highs as WTI rallied past $95.45 (+>1%) on escalating Saudi/Houthi fighting, with Brent above $106; China's September imports +31.0% y/y vs +24.5% expected. Nasdaq-100 winners included Walmart and Vertex (+1%+).
